usedTryThisNowFrames: Choose one organization you admire and write the matched comparison you would need before trusting the lesson: rival, time span, leadership change, and one survival measure.
Pick one task where people still wait for your answer. Write the handoff test: who can perform it tomorrow, using what artifact, while you stay silent.
Name one attractive option in front of you and write the value it would bend. If no value bends, it is not a purpose test.
Take one rule your team defends. Write the core it was meant to protect, then write one different practice that could protect it better now.
Write one large target, then list the three projects it would force you to stop. If it stops nothing, it is probably a slogan.
Pick one value your team claims. Write the behavior that proves it, the behavior that violates it, and what will happen the next time either appears.
Write three small variations for one method you use, one measure that tells whether each served the core, and the date you will kill two of them.
Choose one role that would hurt if vacant tomorrow. Write the three experiences someone inside must complete before they can inherit it.
Find one place where the phrase basically fine appears. Replace it with the visible standard, the smallest unacceptable drift, and who checks it next.
Draw six boxes: core, progress, culture, experiments, leadership, standards. Put one current mechanism in each, and leave blank any box you have not really built.
